transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-25 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 mins
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Sunburst CTO), Marcus Duval (Sunburst ML Eng), Sophie Kim (Sunburst Security)
---
Auto-generated Summary: initial host vs private evaluation, ask for perf parity with existing vLLM stack; action items captured.
Topics: migration path, eval parity, security/KMS, dedicated vs hosted economics, networking/VPC.
Action items: (see metadata)
---
00:00 Alex Moreno: hey everyone thanks for joining, um, i'm alex redwood AE, with priya our systems eng, uh quick round of intro?
00:12 Lena Ortiz: hey uh lena here, CTO at Sunburst, we run real-time analytics and some PII redaction pipelines, so data residency is a must, that's why we're looking at private or dedicated.
00:22 Marcus Duval: Marcus, ML infra, we've been prototyping on vLLM locally and calling OpenAI for some endpoints. looking for cost predictability and run‑time parity.
00:29 Sophie Kim: Sophie, security ops, i'll be asking about audit logs, KMS, and isolation.
00:35 Priya Shah: thanks, i'll be focused on the performance side — latency, kv cache behavior, batching.
00:42 Alex Moreno: high level, Redwood offers hosted api, dedicated capacity, and private vpc/on-prem. today i'd like to understand your current stack and success criteria.
01:05 Lena Ortiz: sure, we use OpenAI for a number of user-facing features, but a good chunk goes through our on-prem vLLM service for cheaper tokens. Some models are TGI forks. Our main pain is unpredictable latency spikes and token costs. also we need SSO integration.
01:29 Alex Moreno: got it. when you say unpredictable latency — are those 95th percentile spikes or steady higher latency for some burst patterns?
01:36 Marcus Duval: mostly p95 spikes during long chat sessions and also when a rare multi-turn prompt hits cold kv cache. vLLM works great for throughput but harder to autoscale for bursty web traffic.
01:50 Priya Shah: mmm mhm — that's where our continuous batching and auto-prefetching for KV cache can help, we also have prefix caching and an adaptive batching policy, it reduces p95 without blowing up cost.
02:10 Marcus Duval: how does that map to TGI/vllm models though? models are often slightly modified — custom tokenizers, small adapter layers.
02:20 Priya Shah: we’ve onboarded many TGI/vLLM variants, runtime will pick kernels based on architecture, and we've got compatibility layers — though occasionally tokenizer name mismatches happen so we do a short manifest step to validate tokenizer and kv shape — it's about the 10 to 20 minute onboarding for most forks.
02:43 Sophie Kim: security — do you offer a customer-managed control plane for private deployments? KMS/HSM support?
02:50 Alex Moreno: yes, Private option gives a customer-managed control plane. we integrate with KMS providers and can support HSM-backed keys for encryption at rest. we also provide audit logs and SSO/SAML for admin access.
03:08 Sophie Kim: retention of logs — we need 2 years for some regs, is that configurable?
03:14 Alex Moreno: configurable retention windows for logs in private and dedicated, hosted by default has a standard retention but enterprise packages can extend.
03:25 Lena Ortiz: cost — what's unit economics compared to OpenAI? even ballpark?
03:31 Alex Moreno: depends on model and quantization, but for large chat style workload we generally see 20-50% cost improving with caching + batching compared to calling public endpoints at scale, and dedicated/reserved contracts give further reductions. we'll send a pricing matrix.
03:50 Marcus Duval: we run custom evals to check parity — do you support running their same prompts and tracking red-team/quality regressions?
03:58 Priya Shah: yes, Redwood Optimize can run eval sets and watch regressions. for the eval parity work we can run your prompt set in our sandbox and return token-by-token diffs and a quality score, plus we can let you run the tests side-by-side against OpenAI/Anthropic to compare.
04:20 Lena Ortiz: the devil's in the details — tokenization mismatches break scoring. how do you handle subtle output diffs during a migration?
04:29 Priya Shah: we add a tokenizer harmonization step in our eval harness, and we let you pin models. for small divergences we provide configurable fallbacks and can route certain low-latency traffic to a smaller hosted model or fall back to your existing vLLM until you're happy.
04:47 Marcus Duval: routing — can we configure policies per-route? eg route billing-sensitive endpoints to dedicated, noisy endpoints to cheaper model variant?
04:54 Alex Moreno: yep, smart routing by policy: latency, cost, region, or customer tier. you can also define canary rules.
05:05 Sophie Kim: network: VPC peering vs private link — what's recommended for reduced blast radius?
05:12 Priya Shah: for private we often recommend interface endpoints and private link equivalents; for on-prem we support direct connect style peering. we can provide a runbook.
05:30 Marcus Duval: ok, about eval perf — priya, what metrics would you capture in the 48h eval?
05:36 Priya Shah: we'll capture 50/90/95/99 latencies, p50 token cost, throughput under various concurrencies, memory/kv hit rates, and effective tokens/sec. we also record tail latency causes.
05:51 Lena Ortiz: curious about model fallout — we use a few custom adapters, is there an easy way to test the adapters without full retrain?
05:59 Priya Shah: yes, we support loading adapter weights and evaluating them in place. often it's a manifest change and small compatibility shim — we'll validate your artifacts in the sandbox.
06:15 Marcus Duval: are there any gotchas when moving from vLLM+TGI to Redwood runtime? we use some experimental CUDA kernels.
06:23 Priya Shah: sometimes micro-optimizations don't translate; in a few cases, custom kernel paths required small changes. we keep a compatibility table and we can do a quick binary check during onboarding to flag those. usually a patch or falling back to a compatible kernel path solves it.
06:40 Alex Moreno: quick note — open to doing a short benchmark where we replicate a slice of your production traffic. that helps quantify cost/latency delta.
06:48 Lena Ortiz: yes please. we'd like to see p95 parity with our current setup and ideally reduce cost.
06:55 Sophie Kim: on compliance, can you show us an example SOC2 report and also outline who has access to logs in hosted vs dedicated vs private?
07:05 Alex Moreno: hosted has limited access and we redact where appropriate; dedicated gives stronger isolation and private gives customer full control. we'll share SOC2 docs and a matrix of access controls.
07:22 Marcus Duval: can we bring our tokenizer artifacts? we have a custom vocabulary and merges file.
07:29 Priya Shah: absolutely — please bundle those into the artifact zip and we'll run the harmonization step.
07:36 Lena Ortiz: timeline — we want to decide by mid march and ideally run a pilot in april.
07:42 Alex Moreno: sounds feasible, we'll align resources.
07:48 (crosstalk) Marcus: also need SSO and RBAC for dev accounts
07:52 Alex: that’s standard — SSO + SAML + RBAC are supported.
08:00 Priya Shah: ok let me walk briefly through a proposed eval plan — step 1: sandbox with your prompt set for 48h, step 2: perf/quality comparison vs OpenAI & vLLM, step 3: joint review and decide hosted vs dedicated vs private pilot.
08:18 Marcus Duval: metrics on step 2 — will you provide token-level cost logs and diffed outputs?
08:23 Priya Shah: yes token-level cost, alignment diffs, and example failure cases.
08:30 Sophie Kim: what about data retention in sandbox, we need scrubbing for PII?
08:36 Alex Moreno: scrub or use redacted dataset; we also offer ephemeral sandboxes with no retention if you prefer.
08:47 Lena Ortiz: ok last question, SLA — what's typical for dedicated?
08:52 Alex Moreno: dedicated comes with guaranteed throughput and latency SLOs; specific numbers are in the contract but we can share sample SLA.
09:03 Priya Shah: any questions we missed?
09:07 Lena Ortiz: none from me — I want the pricing matrix and the security docs.
09:11 Marcus Duval: i'll prepare prompts and the sample dataset slice.
09:15 Sophie Kim: i'll collect the compliance checklist.
09:18 Alex Moreno: great — recap of next steps: we'll send pricing, SOC2/ISO docs, provision sandbox and run the 48h eval once Marcus shares artifacts. schedule deep-dive for networking once security is satisfied.
09:32 Priya Shah: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and slack.
09:36 (meeting ends)
